why: Taking value v earns v times its count but forbids v-1 and v+1, so over the sorted values it is House Robber: you can't take two adjacent values. Group equal values into totals and run the take/skip DP.
hints: After picking v you also lose every v-1 and v+1. Which classic problem forbids taking two neighbours?
Collapse the array to total[v] = v * count(v). Then choose a set of values with no two consecutive integers maximising the sum of total[v]: House Robber over the values.

Walk distinct values in sorted order with take/skip: if v follows the previous value by exactly 1, take = skip_prev + total[v]; otherwise take = best_prev + total[v]. O(n log n), or O(max value) with a bucket array.
pitfalls: Gaps between values matter: if v - 1 is absent, taking v doesn't block the previous value.
All copies of v score together; work with v * count, not v.
